title: Pin transitive actions with workflow lockfiles
summary: GitHub Actions workflow lockfiles are generally available since 2026-10-28 (Free, Team and Enterprise Cloud). `gh actions-lock` writes `.github/workflows/actions.lock`, which records commits for actions and their transitive dependencies, and the runner then runs those recorded commits. A verify mode checks the lockfile in CI without changing files, and admins can turn on a 'Require lockfile' policy. SEC-17's SHA pins cover only the `uses:` lines a workflow writes itself, so dependencies pulled in by those actions still run unpinned today. GitHub notes that a lockfile records what was reviewed; it doesn't make a dependency safe.

amendments.append: Workflows are onboarded to an Actions lockfile (`.github/workflows/actions.lock`, written by `gh actions-lock`), so the actions' transitive dependencies run at recorded commits too. CI checks that the lockfile is current, and in client mode the 'Require lockfile' policy is on. A lockfile records what was reviewed; it doesn't make a dependency safe (SUP-1 still applies).

recommendation.why: It closes the gap SEC-17 leaves open, unpinned transitive actions, with a generally available GitHub feature on every plan this standard targets. The risk is low: the CI check fails only when the lockfile is out of date, and the policy is client-mode only.

acceptOverlaps.SLOG-2~SLOG-4: different duties: SLOG-2 says which security events are logged, SLOG-4 says errors in security checks deny the request (fail closed); they share only the words authentication, authorization, validation
